name: ledger
whenToEnable: Give every player a balance. A per-user ledger for whatever your economy runs on — chips, gold, gems, credits, tokens — in your own D1, currency-agnostic. Every movement is atomic (the ledger entry and the balance change commit together), idempotent (a replayed operation applies once, so a payout delivered twice pays once), and overdraft-safe (a database CHECK constraint makes a balance that can go negative impossible). It has holds — reserve a player's stake the moment a bet is placed, then release it or capture it when the outcome lands — which is what makes wagering safe, so it pairs naturally with @pithy-sh/multiplayer. It takes no position on whether your units map to money; that, and any regulation it implies, is yours. Reads are scoped to the caller; moving another player's balance over HTTP is server-authoritative and needs the admin scope, so add auth too.
scaffold: Add a `ledger({ currencies: [...] })` block to pithy.config.ts and declare at least one currency.
Give each currency a `code` (a lowercase id like `chips`), a `name`, and optionally `decimals` (display scale — balances are always stored as integers in the minor unit).
Bind a D1 database named DB in wrangler.jsonc — the same app database your other capabilities use.
Run `pithy migrate` to create pithy_ledger_accounts, pithy_ledger_transactions, and pithy_ledger_holds.

Add `@pithy-sh/auth` if it is not already installed. Balance reads scope to the authenticated user; admin credit/debit routes need the `ledger:admin` scope. Compose a `resolveScopes` on `@pithy-sh/auth` that answers it for a request your trusted backend proves it sent, never for a player. packages/auth/docs/server-authoritative.md ranks the three proofs.
Move balances in-process from your own code with `openLedger(env.DB)` — credit, debit, transfer, hold, release, capture — passing a unique `ref` for each operation so retries are safe.

Add `controlplane()` if you want a dashboard to read balances and entry logs, and to correct one. `ledger:accounts:read` reads balances and `ledger:transactions:read` the history behind them. `ledger:accounts:adjust` credits, debits, reverses an entry and releases a hold — each with an idempotency key, a required reason and an audit event — and is granted only when you pick it at `pithy dashboard connect`.

configOptions.describe: Every currency this app's ledger holds. Replace this example — one currency is the smallest ledger that does anything, and `chips` is the schema's own first example of a unit that is plainly not money. `code` is a lowercase id, used as a URL path segment and an account key; `name` is what a player sees; optional `decimals` is display scale only, because a balance is always stored as an integer in the minor unit (`decimals: 2` shows a stored 150 as 1.50). At least one currency is required.

The scope a session must carry to credit or debit another player's balance over HTTP. Balance-moving writes are server-authoritative. An attestation about the caller, not a permission granted to the user: resolve it for your own trusted backend through auth's `resolveScopes`, never for a player's device.
